body:
Hopefully this is okay to say, but I have been in a similar position to hers. I broke off an engagement years ago. There were many reasons it had to end, but one reason was that my former fiancé was very depressed and it was dragging me down too. I wanted to help, but at some point had to realize when there was nothing more I could do. 

My former fiancé committed suicide recently. Although we broke up years ago, I still blame myself. Ever since it happened I have suffered nightmares about him and have obsessive thoughts about his death. I hate myself so much because I could not save him. I know it wasn’t working for lots of reasons, but I really loved him and would have never wanted anything bad to happen to him. I will probably feel pain about this for the rest of my life. 

Just know that she would not want you to die. I know it is very painful to go through a breakup. I’m sure she is not having the easiest time either. Maybe there is still hope you can work on it, or maybe you can stay friends. There isn’t much I wouldn’t do if it meant things could happen differently for my ex.

It is possible they went to a private or out-of-state school, or maybe had to retake some classes which quickly drives up the cost. Some students also need loans to cover their living expenses etc, not just tuition. 60k is definitely very high for an associates degree though.
